nonlocal_cap_lattice_radius.law: cap_i = mu sum_j w_ij F_n,j / Z_j over reference-lattice neighbours in contact with the same plane (Oden-Pires type, conservative in total); smode 1
nonlocal_cap_lattice_radius.verdict: REJECTED: partial at mu 0.8 (radius 2 / 3: 0.70 / 0.60 %), mu >= 1.0 not fixed; a lattice radius shrinks under refinement

patch_level_cap.law: cap_i = mu (sum_j F_n,j) m_i / sum_j m_j over the nodes in contact with the same obstacle; smode 6
patch_level_cap.verdict: REJECTED: mu 0.8 passes at n_t 3 / cfl 0.5 but fails at cfl 0.25 (ratio 1.1: 1.16 %), on INC2 (ratio 1.1: D04 0.947) and at mu 0.9; mu >= 1.0 not fixed; hold lost at mu 1.2

patch_cap_lagged_total.law: cap_i = mu L_tau(sum_j F_n,j) m_i / sum_j m_j (patch cap on a first-order-lagged patch normal force); smode 10
patch_cap_lagged_total.verdict: REJECTED: exact at n_t 3 for mu <= 0.95 but not under dx refinement (n_t 4: mu 0.8 ratio 1.1 +1.7 %, mu 0.9 +5.2 %; n_t 6: mu 0.9 +5.2 %), no recovery from a developed flutter, mu >= 1.0 not fixed, holds lost at mu 1.2 / 1.5

symmetric_lag_per_node.law: cap_i = mu F_lag,i, F_lag first-order lag (time constant tau) of the node's normal force, initialised at (re)contact (Prakash-Clifton type normal-stress memory); smode 4
symmetric_lag_per_node.verdict: REJECTED: from rest it removes the flutter (tau 0.5 ms: mu 0.8 exact, also at n_t 4 / INC2; tau 1 / 3 ms: exact to mu 1.2 / 1.5) but (i) it slips under proportional loading: hold ramp-phase displacement 10.5 um at tau 0.5 ms vs 0.19 um for v2 (57x), 37 um + 15 um after the ramp at 1 ms, 0.2-0.5 mm at 3 ms; (ii) it does not recover from a developed flutter (switch at 40 ms: over-friction -12 %); (iii) tau 0.25 ms gives over-friction -7 ... -20 % (the lag holds impact peaks of bouncing nodes): a sharp, geometry-dependent threshold

memory_with_separation.law: cap_i = mu F_lag,i with F_lag relaxing to 0 while the node is out of contact (memory kept across bounces); smode 8 / patch-gated smode 9
memory_with_separation.verdict: REJECTED: friction collapse once nodes bounce (switch at 40 ms: slip error +75 % at mu 1.0; the lagged force averages the zeros of the flight phases), hold slips at tau >= 1 ms; gated: mu 0.8 / 1.0 pass, mu 1.5 collapses (+99 %), hold at mu 1.0 lost

loading_safe_and_gated_memories.verdict: REJECTED: a cap never below the instantaneous one (max) does not suppress the flutter (contact fraction <= 0.04, mu 1.5 +18 %); gating the memory by slip distance or patch macro-slip lets the flutter start before the memory acts and then gives large errors (-15 ... +8 % of g cos theta)

slip_rate_equalisation_patch.law: v2 cap and slider; in SLIP only, outside the cap, a dashpot -2 zd sqrt(k_t m_i)(v_t,i - vbar) on the deviation of the node's realised tangential velocity from the patch mean of the same substep (smode 12: mean over all contact nodes; smode 13: over the nodes whose v2 trial slips, zero net damper force over the slipping set, patch-total friction <= mu sum F_n); zd = 1 removes the whole deviation per substep (2 zd sqrt(kappa_t) = 1)
slip_rate_equalisation_patch.verdict: PROMISING, NOT ADOPTED in X2 (time box): smode 13 zd 1 is exact (|slip err| <= 0.01 %, D04 >= 0.993) for mu 0.6 / 0.8 at n_t 3 / 4 / 6, cfl 0.25 and on INC2, recovers from a developed flutter, keeps v2 hold behaviour (ramp-phase displacement 0.16 um vs 0.19 um for v2; holds at 0.95 mu to mu 1.5 within the stick limit, incl. mu 0.8 at n_t 4 where v2 slides 3.9 mm); mu 1.0 exact at n_t 3 / cfl 0.25 / INC2 but NOT under dx refinement (n_t 4: +2.4 %, n_t 6: +4.2 % at ratio 1.1); mu >= 1.2 sliding fails. It meets the requirement at mu 0.8, not at mu 1.0; it needs a src implementation (two passes, per-patch accumulators, batched layout), pinch / box-frame checks and a declared protocol before any formal claim (task X3)

books_01d_stick_runs.reading: stick runs of v2 (INC, n_t 3): max |B| is the end value B(140 ms) = 2.3-4.3e-12 J against S = 2.2-4.5e-10 J; B rises steadily through the static hold (by 2.0-3.6e-12 J after the ramp, 1.7-3.0e-11 W) and falls only by ~40 % from cfl 0.5 to 0.125 (not first order in dt). The static block keeps a sustained jitter (v_rms 5-12 um/s, growing as dt shrinks) that the contact dashpots dissipate (net contact work -1.6e-11 ... -1.3e-10 W in the hold); the B drift is the part of that dissipation not matched by a booked energy change. It is a genuine residual of the discrete dynamics more than 10 orders of magnitude above the float64 resolution of the books sums (~1e-26 J here): an absolute floor tied to float64 resolution would not change any verdict, and the relative criterion is not measuring float64 noise. Its weakness for static rows is structural (the residual accumulates with the hold duration while S stays fixed), which argues for a drift-rate criterion derived a priori, not for relabelling the residual. No rule is declared (no v3 run); the -01 d FAIL of contact_v2_001 stands
